disclaimer.title: Safety Disclaimer
disclaimer.description:
## ⚠️ Remote Infrared Heater Control — Disclaimer

**WARNING:** Using this integration to remotely control an infrared heater may create a fire hazard and could result in property damage, serious injury, or death.

---

### Important Safety Notice

By installing, enabling, configuring, or using any integration, automation, software, hardware, script, application, or service that allows the remote control of an infrared heater, you acknowledge and accept that remotely operating a heating device introduces significant safety risks.

Remote control of heating equipment should only be used with devices that are specifically designed, certified, and approved by their manufacturer for unattended and remote operation. Using remote control functions with equipment not intended for such use may significantly increase the risk of fire, injury, property damage, equipment damage, or other hazardous conditions.

### Potential Risks and Hazards

The user understands and acknowledges that remote activation of an infrared heater may result in, but is not limited to:

- Fire hazards resulting from flammable materials being located too close to the heater.
- Overheating of surrounding objects, furniture, fabrics, curtains, paper, or other combustible materials.
- Property damage caused by malfunction, incorrect configuration, software defects, hardware defects, communication failures, or user error.
- Personal injury, burns, or harm to occupants, visitors, children, pets, or third parties.
- Damage resulting from loss of network connectivity, power interruptions, equipment failures, automation errors, sensor failures, or unexpected device behavior.
- Activation of the heater when the premises are unattended.
- Failure of safety mechanisms, thermostats, sensors, relays, or any component involved in the control system.
- Risks arising from unauthorized access, hacking, cybersecurity incidents, or compromised user accounts.
- Operation contrary to manufacturer recommendations, safety instructions, certifications, or intended use.
- Any other direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, special, or punitive damages arising from the use or misuse of the system.

### User Responsibility

The user acknowledges that:

1. They are solely responsible for determining whether remote control of the heater is safe and appropriate for their specific environment.
2. They have verified that the heater is suitable for remote and unattended operation and that such operation does not violate any manufacturer instructions, warnings, certifications, local regulations, insurance requirements, or applicable laws.
3. They have reviewed and will comply with all manufacturer instructions, warnings, safety guidelines, local regulations, and applicable laws.
4. They have taken appropriate precautions to minimize the risk of fire, injury, property damage, and equipment damage.
5. They understand that no software, automation platform, integration, hardware component, or control system can guarantee safe operation under all circumstances.
6. They assume all risks associated with the installation, configuration, operation, and use of the system.

### Release of Liability

To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, the user agrees that the authors, developers, contributors, maintainers, distributors, publishers, installers, integrators, and any other parties associated with the integration or software shall not be held liable for any loss, damage, injury, claim, expense, cost, or liability arising from or related to: the use or inability to use the integration; remote operation of the heater; incorrect configuration or deployment; hardware or software failures; cybersecurity incidents; user negligence or misuse; use of equipment not designed or certified for remote operation; or any direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, special, punitive, or exemplary damages.

### Indemnification

The user agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the authors, developers, contributors, maintainers, distributors, publishers, installers, integrators, and associated parties from and against any and all claims, liabilities, damages, losses, costs, expenses, and legal fees arising from or relating to the user's installation, configuration, operation, or use of the integration and any remotely controlled heating equipment.

settings.title: Heater control and safety
settings.description: Choose one heating controller. With Luxeva climate control, select a room sensor for temperature regulation, or leave it empty for manual level control. Disable any Generic Thermostat helper controlling this heater before switching to Luxeva climate. Actuator control is for an external thermostat helper. Saving ends the current heating session and leaves heating off. For local control, first add a separate Local MQTT service entry, then select it here. The upstream switch must be a separate plug or relay rated for this heater; power is never restored automatically.

data.sensor_timeout_minutes: Maximum sensor reading age (minutes; 0 disables age checking)
data.protect_external_starts: Apply a safety timer to heating started by the remote or app

local_service.title: Local MQTT service
local_service.description: Configure a shared local MQTT service once, then select it for any number of heater entries. On HA OS, core-mosquitto is the usual internal hostname. Other installations need an existing broker. Automatic preparation requires Supervisor; it preserves other logins but may restart Mosquitto and briefly disconnect other MQTT devices. The supplied login was observed on the tested heater; other firmware may differ. You must redirect iot.luxeva.com.tr to the broker LAN address in your network DNS. A successful broker check does not yet prove the heater has been redirected. Custom ACLs must allow native MAC-based inTopic, outTopic and OTA_Ready topics.

data.prepare_mosquitto: Install/configure Mosquitto and provision the heater login (may restart the broker)

data_description.prepare_mosquitto: If Mosquitto is already installed, this only adds the heater login when it is missing and keeps all other logins and settings.

error.invalid_mac: Invalid MAC address. Use the format XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX (e.g. 00:AA:11:BB:22:CC).
error.disclaimer_not_accepted: You must read and accept the disclaimer to continue.
error.local_service_required: Add a Local MQTT service entry first, then choose it here.
error.invalid_power_switch: Choose a physical upstream power switch, not a Luxeva actuator.
error.cannot_connect: Could not authenticate to the broker. Check its address, port, credentials and whether it is running.
error.broker_setup_failed: Could not prepare Mosquitto. Check Supervisor availability, broker logs and existing login conflicts; or configure the broker manually.
error.reset_safety_first: Reset safety shutdown before changing or removing the upstream power switch.
error.broker_in_use: A Local MQTT service already uses this broker address and port.

progress.prepare_broker: Preparing Mosquitto if requested, then checking MQTT authentication. This may take a few minutes.

local_connection.title: Waiting for local heater status
local_connection.description: No fresh local status has been received for heater {mac}. Redirect iot.luxeva.com.tr to the LAN address of broker {broker}, allow TCP 1883 from the heater network, and provision its MQTT login. Permit inTopic/{mac}, outTopic/{mac} and OTA_Ready/{mac} in custom ACLs. The heater may need to reconnect after a DNS change. This issue clears when a fresh device status arrives.

local_service_missing.title: Local MQTT service is missing
local_service_missing.description: The local service selected for heater {mac} was removed or is invalid. Choose another Local MQTT service in the heater Configure flow. Heating is unavailable; the safety shutdown controls remain accessible. There is no automatic cloud fallback.
